title_en: GTA 6 Weather Still Not Varied Even After the Patch? PS5 Players Are Sharing a Method That May Help Rain and Thunderstorms Kick In
summary_en: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
body_en:
Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
Lack of weather variety was something I noticed myself during the game’s review period, but Rockstar deployed a small fix during that time too. It was hard to tell whether it was working as intended because the weather also grows more stark as you move through the game.
“The weather types change throughout each day, and the overall weather pattern changes per chapter, evolving from generally very good weather in the first chapter to much more changeable and stormy in the last chapter,” said Owen Shepherd, vice president of art: lighting and rendering at Rockstar, when I asked.
“This is analogous to Florida’s weather patterns in winter through to summer autumn. During the first chapters there are pockets of rain but due to the localization of weather it is possible to miss these."
However, it seems like the issue persisted into the live version of the game, blurring the line between thematically appropriate and accurate weather patterns and unintended bug. The latest patch fixed this for the most part, but some players found they were still experiencing minimal weather changes.
If you’re having the same issue, there might be a fix (discovered by X / Twitter user @mauricioce85796 ). On PS5, you need to turn off your console and boot it into safe mode by holding the power button down until it beeps.
From there, choose option six and select “clear system cache.” According to people who have tested it, this forces the patch to do its job.
“I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather,” said Rockstar fan account Gameroll . “I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted.”
Of course, this could be a placebo, but players in the replies have been trying it and immediately seeing results. “Guys, I can confirm, it’s working,” said one happy X / Twitter user who showcased a rainy clip. “Can confirm, weather is more varied!” said another .
Clearing your cache on PS5 won’t delete game saves or installed games. It just deletes temporary system files and lets the console recreate fresh ones without erasing your games, saved data, screenshots, or account settings. It helps resolve system feature glitches, slow performance, stuttering, app or game launch errors, and network or sync hiccups. People have been doing it for years, claiming to see performance benefits as a result.
